it is perfectly pervasive, exhausting all of space within every dust-mote world; its imperial jewels are vast and expansive, encompassing [all things].
Within a single hair-tip,
the Dharma-realm is unimpededly fused and integrated— the wondrous realm of Vairocana;
where limits once existed, they have vanished— this is the profound discernment of Samantabhadra’s eye.
The vast and profound subtle words are indeed difficult to fathom in their ultimate intent;
the expansive and deep ocean of Dharma is especially rare for its source to be measured.
Now, I shall briefly set forth the general outline by opening these ten meanings.
I have extracted the essential points and titled this work *Zhigui* (The Essential Return), so that those who seek the profound mysteries may gain a rough understanding of its ultimate intent.

Explaining the Place Where the Sūtra Was Spoken, Part One:** Now, when the Perfect Teaching arises, it necessarily pervades all directions throughout the world of dust.
Since this discourse concerns the entirety of the Dharma-realm,
how could its locations be divided?
For now, proceeding from the narrow to the broad, I shall briefly open up ten locations.
First, this Jambudvīpa;
second, ten billion worlds;
third, throughout the ten directions.
Fourth, it pervades all sensory objects;
fifth, it penetrates different realms;
sixth, it encompasses individual objects.
Seventh, returning to the Flower Treasury;
eighth, the layered gathering of lands;
ninth, like a net of Indra.
The ten or more Buddhas are the same.
Regarding "this Jambudvīpa" at the beginning:
it refers to these seven locations and eight assemblies, such as the Bodhi tree in this Jambudvīpa.
Regarding the statement that this Dharma of the sutra was taught "twice over ten billion [worlds]":
this refers to the entirety of these ten billion Jambudvīpas within the Sahā world-system, including the kings of the Jambu trees and so forth.
They are spoken of simultaneously.
"Pervading the ten directions" means pervading the entirety of the ten directions of empty space and the dharma-realm.
In all the realms of Mount Sumeru,
there is not one where this Dharma is not taught simultaneously,
as described in the "Chapter on the Awakening of Radiance."
Regarding the fourth, the path of pervading all particles:
this means that within the space-element of the ten directions,
at the location of every single particle, there exists one of those buddha-fields.
Within all of these, he preached this sutra to those of the five supernormal powers in various realms—
namely, in diverse classes of worlds such as those shaped like trees—
and to others numbering as many as the atoms within unspeakable Buddha-fields.
Each and every stream of similar types pervades the ten directions of empty space and the dharma-realm;
they are equal to the aforementioned realm of Mount Sumeru,
yet they do not obstruct one another.
In each of these, he turns the sublime Wheel of Dharma.
Regarding the phrase "the six encompassing individual particles":
this refers to every single particle-path throughout the entirety of the realm of empty space.
Each of these likewise encompasses, as before, an immeasurable ocean of lands of its own kind,
and within them this sutra is also preached.
Seventh is the Return to the Flower Treasury.
This means that all these various defiled worlds are each equally exhausted;
they are exclusively the Lotus Treasury Adorned World-Ocean, numbering more than the atoms within a buddha-field,
each of which completely pervades the entire dharma-realm without mutual obstruction.
In all of these, he expounds this Dharma.
Regarding the "eightfold array of lands," within every single atom of this Flower Treasury World (*kusumatalagarbha-lokadhātu*), [he does so].
All encompass the boundless oceans of Buddha-fields,
and within each of them, this Dharma of the sutra is preached.
"The ninth is like Indra’s net" means:
Since each and every one of those atoms individually encompasses this ocean of infinite lands,
there are further atoms within these very lands and so forth.
Within each of those atoms there are further oceans of lands;

so too are these lands infinite.
Just as in Indra’s net, each layer possesses ten times that which is unspeakable; such is its magnitude.
All that has been described above constitutes the place where Vairocana Buddha preached the Avataṃsaka Sūtra.

Answer: This refers to the location of the Trāyastriṃśa Heaven within the ten stages (daśabhūmi).

Thus, the ten stages (*daśabhūmi*) were taught throughout such realms as the Yāma heaven and the Trāyastriṃśa heaven;

Question: According to what has been stated here, the assembly of the Avataṃsaka Sūtra is said to have no end at all;
how, then, could there exist this single volume of scriptural teaching?
Answer: It is for the sake of inferior sentient beings that these [teachings] were briefly extracted from the inexhaustible discourse and compiled for circulation.
There is this one section which,
through the skillful means of being seen or heard,
leads them into the boundless and limitless.
Just as one perceives boundless space through a crack in a window,
know that the principle herein is likewise:
by observing this single section, one beholds the boundless ocean of dharmas.
Furthermore, this very section concludes with a general application that spans an ocean of boundless eons,
for the text contains no fixed limits.
Because a single teaching is itself all teachings.
Question: If he has been teaching thus constantly throughout these many eons, for what reason does the Tathāgata enter parinirvāṇa?
The answer states that, according to this sutra, the Buddha never enters parinirvāṇa;

Furthermore, the Buddha Vairocana constantly dwells within the Flower Treasury World (Gandavyūha),
